prompt:
Create ONE original transparent RGBA PNG production sprite sheet for ASHVEIL, a bleak earth-toned survival RPG. This is a sheet of EMPTY GARMENT OBJECTS ONLY, no wearer, no person, no skin, no anatomical limbs, no hands or feet, no weapons, no mannequin. These are NEW original wearable garment panels, not inventory miniatures and not any other game's pixels.

Use the TWO supplied OWN PROJECT references only:
REFERENCE 1 is the project's neutral-body component pilot. It gives a broad adult torso's proportions, straight neutral posture, restrained detailed pixel-painted fabric, and top-down RPG camera. IMPORTANT: its row 2 torso actually faces VIEWER RIGHT and its row 3 torso actually faces VIEWER LEFT. Do not blindly copy those incorrect requested row names. Study the actual visible surfaces. Ignore its limbs entirely; do not paint any skin or wearer into this output.
REFERENCE 2 is the project's existing equipment inventory atlas. Use ONLY its material identities: faded gray-beige rag linen, worn dark umber leather with dull metal fastenings, dark iron linked chain mail, ash-gray cloth hood. Do not paste or enlarge its little inventory icons.

EXACT layout: FOUR ROWS and FOUR COLUMNS = exactly SIXTEEN isolated original garment objects, one object per cell. Prefer a square high-resolution2048x2048 canvas with wide completely transparent gutters. Keep every object centered in its own cell, fully visible, roughly220 source pixels high for the shirt torso panel; the coat body may be longer and hood shorter in natural proportions. No object may touch a cell edge or its neighbor. No row/column labels, numbers, text, drawn grid, decorations, platform, cast shadow, fog, glow, colored backdrop, loose debris, spare objects or detached duplicates.

All objects are shown upright and in the SAME neutral standing orientation as the reference body, with no leaning action pose. FOUR authored directional rows, NEVER a mirrored or mixed view within a row:
ROW1: FRONT, toward viewer: front neckline/fastenings and hood face aperture.
ROW2: LEFT, actual profile pointing toward VIEWER LEFT. Show the near side that naturally belongs to this profile, front garment edge toward image left.
ROW3: RIGHT, actual profile pointing toward VIEWER RIGHT. Show the opposite actual side, front garment edge toward image right.
ROW4: BACK, away from viewer: back seams/panels and hood back cloth. NO new front-face aperture on the BACK hood, no front coat fastening stripe on the back.

The FOUR columns are consistent in EVERY row:
COLUMN1: Rag linen SHORT-SLEEVE SHIRT TORSO PANEL ONLY. Faded gray-beige rag cloth, believable stitch repairs, hem ending at natural waist. Entire torso body panel from open neck to waist, NO sleeves; retain clean empty arm-socket cutouts for later independent upper-arm sleeves. No shoulder skin caps or arm stumps. Transparent neck aperture and outside silhouette where appropriate. Do NOT include shorts/pelvis/legs or an undershirt wearer.
COLUMN2: WORN LEATHER COAT BODY PANEL ONLY. Dark brown aged leather, restrained dull fastenings, fitted chest/abdomen and waist, separated lower front/back coat hem reaching upper thighs. No arms or sleeves; clear arm sockets for later independent sleeve parts. FRONT has practical front opening/fastenings; BACK is actual back panels and seam. No hand, skin, trousers, or legs visible inside. Do not bake detached sleeve shapes into the torso body.
COLUMN3: IRON CHAIN-MAIL TORSO PANEL ONLY. Small readable dark iron links over a subtle dark cloth edge binding, collar/neck and natural waist hem. No arms, sleeves, legs, wearer or separate shoulder pads. Open neck and arm sockets appropriate to visible direction. Front and back surfaces must be physically plausible mail surfaces; do not draw a human chest underneath.
COLUMN4: OPAQUE CLOTH HOOD / COWL SHELL ONLY. A separate empty ash-gray worn cloth hood with short neck/shoulder cowl. Front and profile views have a true transparent EMPTY FACE APERTURE (no face, eyes, nose, skin, skull or black painted mannequin). Back view shows opaque actual back hood cloth. Neck opening and hem belong to the garment shell only. Cloth itself remains opaque with folds and stitched edging; do not make a glowing transparent ghost cloth.

Detailed restrained pixel-painted material work with large readable silhouettes at small RPG map scale, crisp texture and limited earthy palette. Main lit cloth/leather/metal mass should be opaque, edges antialiased naturally, background fully transparent. Maintain one matching body scale and collar/waist construction across each garment's four rows. Keep all SIXTEEN objects complete and cleanly separated. No full outfitted body, no full costume with baked sleeves, no whole character animation, no additional items.
